To: Executive Supply Chain Team
From: Sustainability & Logistics Director
Subject: Balancing Transportation Cost and Carbon — Route Activation and Flow Plan
Date: [Insert date]

Context
Our outbound network moves product from multiple warehouses to multiple stores. Each possible shipping route carries two critical metrics: a dollar cost per unit and a CO2 emission rate per unit. In practice, the least expensive routes are often the most carbon-intensive, creating a direct trade-off between financial efficiency and our sustainability commitments. We need a single, pragmatic plan that meets store needs, respects warehouse limits, and delivers the best overall outcome across cost and carbon.

Operational rules and real-world constraints
- Route activation costs: Starting any route imposes a one-time setup expense (e.g., carrier onboarding, paperwork, dock configuration). A route is either active or inactive; once active, this setup cost is incurred regardless of volume shipped on that lane.
- Minimum order quantities: Activated routes must move at least a defined number of units. This reflects full-truck economics and handling requirements; partial loads are not accepted on newly activated lanes.
- Supplier limits per store: Each store can receive from only a limited number of warehouses to avoid dock congestion, reduce scheduling complexity, and align with vendor policies. This cap is part of our planning rules.

Supply and demand parameters
- Each warehouse has a finite volume available for shipment. We cannot exceed available inventory.
- Each store has a minimum demand that must be met in full within the planning horizon.
- The plan must respect both the outbound capacities at warehouses and the required inbound volumes at stores.

Management priority and how we will score plans
To translate the cost-versus-carbon trade-off into clear direction, we will score every feasible shipping plan using management’s weights for cost and emissions. Specifically, we will:
- Apply the cost weight to the total variable shipping dollars across all active routes.
- Apply the emission weight to the total CO2 emitted across all shipments.
- Add the full setup costs for any activated routes without weighting.
The blended score reflects our financial and environmental priorities while fully accounting for activation expenses.

Business goal
Identify which routes to activate and how much to ship on each active route so that:
- Warehouse inventories are not exceeded.
- Each store’s demand is met in full.
- Any activated route ships at least the minimum order quantity.
- Each store receives from no more than the allowed number of warehouses.
- The resulting blended total (weighted variable cost, weighted emissions, plus full setup costs) is as low as possible within these operational rules.

Deliverables
- Recommended set of activated routes and shipment volumes by lane.
- Confirmation that all operational rules and supply/demand limits are met.
- Scenario insights showing how the plan shifts if cost/emission weights or supplier limits change.
- Notable trade-offs where a lower cost would materially increase emissions, or vice versa.
